subject: biology-2
question: Which of the following statements best contrasts **spermatogenesis** with **oogenesis** in humans?

options.text: Oogenesis produces four functional gametes per meiotic cycle, while spermatogenesis produces one.
Both processes pause in prophase of meiosis I until puberty.
Spermatogenesis begins before birth, while oogenesis continues throughout life.
Spermatogenesis produces four functional sperm from one primary spermatocyte, while oogenesis produces one ovum and polar bodies from one primary oocyte.

explanation: Each primary spermatocyte yields four functional sperm, whereas each primary oocyte yields a single ovum plus polar bodies, preserving the cytoplasm the egg needs. A reverses those numbers, attributing four gametes to oogenesis. B fails because spermatogenesis runs continuously from puberty and does not pause in prophase of meiosis I. C reverses the timing, since oogenesis begins before birth and spermatogenesis begins at puberty.
